common_name: Green Jewel Coneflower (Unusual Solid Green-Flowered Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun. Green Jewel is a striking coneflower cultivar producing unusual, solid apple-green ray petals surrounding a darker green central cone, an unusual and much sought-after color departure from the typical purple, pink, and orange tones of most coneflower cultivars. It blooms over a long summer season and, like other coneflowers, is drought-tolerant and low-maintenance once established, drawing butterflies and bees despite its unconventional color. Leaving spent seed heads standing through winter provides food for goldfinches and other seed-eating birds.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun. Green Envy produces distinctive flowers that open a soft lime-green and gradually develop pink-rose tips and undersides as they age, giving each bloom a shifting bicolor effect not seen in typical coneflower cultivars. It blooms over a long summer season, tolerates heat and drought well once established, and draws butterflies and bees like other coneflowers despite its unusual coloring. Leaving spent flower heads standing through winter provides valuable seed for goldfinches and other birds.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun. Green Twister produces rosy-pink ray petals edged in lime-green at the tips, creating a distinctive two-toned pinwheel effect around a dark orange-brown central cone, a striking color combination among modern coneflower cultivars. It blooms over a long summer season and shares the classic coneflower traits of drought tolerance, heat tolerance, and low maintenance once established, drawing bees and butterflies throughout its bloom period. Leaving the seed heads standing through winter provides food for goldfinches and adds structural interest to the dormant garden.

common_name: Coconut Lime Coneflower (Double Green-and-White Pompom Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean to moderately fertile soil in full sun. Coconut Lime produces fully double, pompom-like flowers combining a creamy white outer ring of petals with a raised, shaggy lime-green center, an unusual double form and color combination quite different from the simple single daisy flowers of the wild species. Its novel double form makes it a strong focal point in a mixed border and a good cut flower, though like other double coneflower cultivars it can be somewhat shorter-lived than the straight species and benefits from sharp drainage, particularly through humid summers. It still draws some pollinators, though double flowers generally offer less accessible pollen and nectar than single-flowered coneflower types.

common_name: American Gold Rush Rudbeckia (Disease-Resistant Fuzzy-Leaved Black-Eyed Susan)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring in well-drained, average soil in full sun; American Gold Rush was named Perennial Plant of the Year for its outstanding resistance to Septoria leaf spot, a common fungal disease that disfigures many black-eyed Susan cultivars in humid climates.

directions: Plant in well-drained, average soil in full sun. American Gold Rush was named the Perennial Plant Association's Perennial Plant of the Year for its exceptional resistance to Septoria leaf spot and other fungal diseases that commonly disfigure black-eyed Susan foliage in hot, humid climates, staying attractive through the entire growing season where older cultivars decline. It produces abundant golden-yellow flowers with a distinctive dark red-brown ring around the central cone, held above narrow, softly fuzzy, silver-green foliage that adds textural interest even before bloom. It is drought-tolerant once established, blooms over a long summer season, and provides valuable seed for goldfinches if spent flower heads are left standing into winter.
